chat_messages.text: I want to grow tomatoes on a north-facing balcony in Hamburg. Is that hopeless?

content.text: I want to grow tomatoes on a north-facing balcony in Hamburg. Is that hopeless?

chat_messages.text: Not hopeless, but pick your battles. North-facing in Hamburg means maybe 3–4 hours of indirect light in summer. Cherry and currant tomatoes tolerate that far better than large slicing varieties. Use the lightest-coloured wall you have as a reflector and keep the pots as close to the railing as possible.

chat_messages.text: Three that people report doing well in low light: 'Red Robin' (dwarf, 30 cm), 'Tumbling Tom' (trailing, good for a railing box), and 'Zuckertraube' (a German cherry type that ripens early). Start them indoors in early April.

content.text: 我决定种 Zuckertraube 和 Tumbling Tom。花盆要多大?

chat_messages.text: Zuckertraube 至少 15 升一株,Tumbling Tom 放栏杆箱里 8–10 升就够。两种都别和别的植物挤一个盆,北阳台光已经少了,根再抢水就更慢。记得我们说的:盆贴着栏杆放。
